Baseline reddit's thumbnailling system worked by basically taking the first image present in the HTML code of the linked-to website. This usually worked for both image links themselves (it'd give you a thumbnail of the image) and news articles (usually the first image would be the logo of the newspaper).

This didn't ALWAYS work but exceptions are exceptions for a reason.

The real problem comes when you don't want the first image to be the thumbnail. For example, if reddit's thumbnailling system were used on that link that you posted (to flickr), it'd just show you flickr's logo.

RES is specifically set up to circumvent this:

http://www.reddit.com/r/test/comments/32iar1/test_poast_please_ignoar/

As you can see, RES appears to have specific protocols for handling Flickr links. It's implausible for a website itself to implement this (RES can do it because RES doesn't really need to do much else). In the meantime, direct links will always work.

Well, if you really want to be technical about it, given a limited space no matter how small the growth rate eventually whatever is growing will outgrow the space on a timescale of forever.

But I suppose you are correct, given a low enough growth rate, technically, growth can continue near indefinitely. But there functionally a cut off point where growth is so slow that it can't reasonably be counted as growth in any meaningful way.

Take a look at these growth rates converted to doubling times. Just in general for the concept of growth.

0.1% growth = doubling time of 700 years

0.5% growth = doubling time of 140 years

1% growth = doubling time of 70 years

2% growth = doubling time of 35 years

3% growth = doubling time of 23.33 years

4% growth = doubling time of 17.5 years

5% growth = doubling time of 14 years

The current human population growth rate is about 1.14% and the current human population is about 7,236,576,000.

Even at a 0.1% growth over the next year we would add over 7 million people to the planet, 7 million people require a lot of resources and infrastructure. Over the next 50 years we would add over 370 million people to the planet (more than the entire population of the US), and over the next 100 years we would add over 760 million people.

At 0.5% over the next year we would add over 36 million people, over the next 50 years we would add over 2 billion people, and over the next 100 years we would add over 4.6 billion people.

And at current growth rates of 1.14% over the next year we would add 82 million people, over the next 50 years we would add over 5.5 billion people, and over the next 100 years we would add over 15 billion people.

And in the grand scheme of things 100 years is nothing.

I support body cameras with a few stipulations. They cant be turned off by the police officer. They record and report evidence of malfunction back at the station, so that an officer may not proceed lawfully without them recording. They must be head mounted to record the officers perspective. The footage needs to be made available immediately, without editing, upon complaint.

Too many cases have already been seen of either officers turning off the camera or it miraculously temporarily 'malfunctions' when going rogue. Head mounted would also address whether or not an officer saw someone reach for a weapon or act threateningly; where as a chest mounted camera could be facing away.
